the introduction of profit sharing is followed by a statistically significant, positive change in productivity and that the size of the change is positively related to the proportion of employees who participate in the profit-sharing plan.

1) the introduction of profit sharing is accompanied by a statistically significant and positive change in productivity; 2) this change in productivity is larger for firms in which a higher proportion of employees are covered by the plan; and 3) the effect of profit sharing on productivity is robust across a wide variety of model specifications, and is not explained by changes in personnel policies or management practices.
